parties:
Pubali Bank Ltd ------ Appellant
vs
Farzana Begum and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Khondker Musa Khaled J: This First Appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 26-2-1994 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (Joint District Judge,) Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 209 of 1990 dismissing the suit. 

 5. The learned Judge of the trial Court framed five issues and during the trial she recorded evidence of only one PW. The defendant No. 1 was, however, examined on commission as DW 1. At the instance of PW 1 series of documents were made Exhibit Nos. 1-15 against none by the defendant. The learned Subordinate Judge found dissimilarities in between signatures of defendant No. 1 as available on various exhibited documents and due to such dissimilarities, she came to the finding that the defendant No. 1 did not actually open the CC. Account No. 69 and that her husband received the loan money by forging her signatures in connivance with some Bank employees. Since the defendant No. 1 did not receive loan, the learned Judge held the view that she should not be made liable to pay the money. Accordingly, the suit was dismissed by the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-2-1994. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiff-Bank preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Subordinate Judge has erroneously arrived at a wrong decision in dismissing the suit and that she could not appreciate the evidence on the record in the right direction. 

 7. Mr Zakir Hussain Muzumder, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the defendant No. 1 did not intentionally identify her admitted signatures out of the exhibited documents. But she tried to deny each and every one in spite of her admission regarding execution of some documents by putting signatures. Even if all the signatures of the defendant appearing on the documents are not found similar, such difference might have been caused intentionally or it might also occur due to the long time gap from one to other. But for that reason, it is totally wrong to arrive at a positive finding that the defendant No. 1 did not receive loan money from the Bank by opening CC Account No. 69. The learned Advocate submits further that the learned Subordinate Judge could at best reduce some penal interest from the amount claimed, but dismissal of the entire claim of money was illegal and it cannot be sustainable in law. He submits that admittedly the defendant No. 1 knew about the demand notice for payment of loan and on one occasion, she went to the Bank with her husband, but she did not inform the matter to the Bank that she did not take loan by opening any account. Rather, she had fully endorsed and acknowledged the loan which stood in her name at the relevant time. In fact, she enjoyed the loan with her husband, but denied it cunningly on this or that plea. Therefore, he prays for setting aside the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and decreeing the suit. 

 14. However, the learned Advocate for the appellant has made submission that the amount of Taka 5,09,340.50 as claimed by the Bank by adding penal interest on the said amount may create hardship and, as such, it may be reduced to a reasonable amount in view of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. We also find that the claim of Taka 5,09,34050 becomes very high against the small loan amount of Taka 40,000 and it will create hardship to refund. So the amount of claim may be reduced according to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, which allows the Bank to set up claim of only the loan amount by adding not more than double the principle amount as interest irrespective of the contract. In the said line, we consider it fit and proper to pass a part decree against the defendants for the principal loan amounting to Taka 40,000 plus double the said amount i.e. 80,000 as interest making a total Taka 1,20,000 only. 

 16. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 209 of 1990 are set aside. The original suit is decreed in part in preliminary form with cost against the defendant No. 1 and without cost against the rest. The defendant No. 1 is directed to pay Taka 1,20,000 to the plaintiff-Bank within three months from this date, failing which, the plaintiff-Bank shall be able to sell out the mortgage property and realise the same through the process of law.
